title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂ = Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. Ĝ^+_{0,3} is the extension of G_3 ≅ S_3 by Π̂ (the orbifold group of the quotient by S_3). In it:
- σ_∞ is an involution fixing ∞ and swapping 0 and 1.
- ρ is an element of order 3 permuting 0, 1, ∞ cyclically.
- l_0, l_1, l_∞ are the inertia generators.
- l_0' = ε_0 = σ_∞ρ generates the inertia of the orbifold point above 0, with ε_0^2 = l_0. So L_0' = ε_0^{Ẑ} ⊃ L_0 = l_0^{Ẑ}.

Previous page. An outer automorphism u of Ĝ^+ that induces the identity on G_3, fixes σ_∞, fixes ρ mod Π̂, and respects the conjugacy class of loop subgroups is shown to be equivalent to data (g_0 mod L_0, ν ∈ Ẑ). The derivation uses N_Π̂(L_1) = L_1 and u(L_0) = int(g_0)(L_0) (42).

This page.
- u is given by (36): u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ, with g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1}.
- The only constraint needed for u to define a homomorphism is (38), (gρ)^3 = 1, i.e. g·ρ(g)·ρ^2(g) = 1.
- Grothendieck then checks that the inertia condition (42), and even the stronger (43) u(L_0') ⊂ int(g_0)(L_0'), holds automatically. Since σ_∞σ_∞(g_0) = g_0σ_∞ and ρ(g_0)^{-1}ρ = ρg_0^{-1}, one has u(σ_∞ρ) = σ_∞gρ = g_0(σ_∞ l_1^ν ρ)g_0^{-1}.
- Next, σ_∞ l_1^ν ρ = (σ_∞ l_1^ν σ_∞)(σ_∞ρ) = l_0^ν ε_0 = ε_0^{2ν+1}.
- Hence int(g_0^{-1})u(ε_0) = ε_0^{2ν+1}. A first crossed-out attempt worked with the squares l_0 = ε_0^2 and got the same exponent.

Next page. Setting p = 2ν+1 gives u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^p). Grothendieck checks that any p ∈ Ẑ* is odd, so (p−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ. Rewriting (38) with h_0 = σ_∞(g_0)^{-1}g_0 yields the boxed relation (46), (l_0^ν h_0^{-1})·ρ(…)·ρ^2(…) = 1. This is the 'pentagon-free' Grothendieck–Teichmüller pair: (λ = p, f ↔ h_0) with the 2-cycle relation coming from σ_∞-equivariance and the 3-cycle relation with exponent m = (λ−1)/2.

Purpose. The page re-derives, from S_3-equivariant automorphisms of the orbifold group Π̂_{0,3} ⋊ S_3, the defining relations of what is now called (the 'GT_0' part of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, which he had already called relation (10) earlier in the Longue Marche.
errors: No mathematical error found. Each step (σ_∞σ_∞(g_0) = g_0σ_∞, σ_∞l_1σ_∞ = l_0, l_0 = ε_0^2) checks, up to the orientation/sign conventions for σ_∞(l_1) = l_0, which are not stated on the page.
Minor notational drift: the exponent is written ν on the previous page and looks like γ here; the next page's transcription has q_0 where the image has g_0.

missed.claim: This is an explicit derivation of the GT 2-/3-cycle relations from automorphisms of the S_3-orbifold extension Π̂_{0,3} ⋊ S_3. It shows that the inertia-preservation condition (via the orbifold half-loop ε_0 = σ_∞ρ) is automatic and forces λ = 2ν+1. This predates Drinfeld but is consistent with, and largely recovered by, the later literature (Lochak–Schneps). It also restates material already in La Longue Marche. It adds no new result, only a documented early orbifold-style derivation.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: documents Grothendieck's orbifold-group (S_3-extension) route to GT relations, including the role of half-loops at orbifold points.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine verification within Grothendieck's known pre-Drinfeld derivation of GT-type relations. The relations themselves (his relation (10)) are already in La Longue Marche, and the orbifold viewpoint was later developed in the literature.
